name: nazar-andriievych/ukraine-air-alerts-analysis
type: repo (student / cohort peer project, same KSE Agentic AI School Stage 2 task)
year: 2026 (created 2026-10-12 08:48 UTC, last push 2026-10-12 17:36 UTC, deadline day; 12 commits on main incl. merged 'weather' branch)
peer_review_status: student repo, self-reported results; not peer reviewed
target_type: STATE target, not onset: label = 1 if the raion was under alert at any moment in the UTC hour. 24% of raion-hours are positive overall, 34% in the test weeks. No at-risk masking, so the +1 h gain is mostly 'an ongoing alert continues'. The author states this limitation openly: the models 'rarely foresee when a new alert starts'. Not directly comparable to our onset target (D-020 estimand).
target_definition: Unit = raion x UTC hour. Origin = end of hour t (the full hour t is known). Horizons h = 1..24: the hour starting at origin + (h-1) h. y = 1 if any alert (union of oblast/raion/hromada alerts mapped to that raion) is active at any moment in that hour. Multi-horizon (24 outputs) probability forecast. An earlier target (daily alert hours per raion, next 7 days) was dropped.
spatial_unit: raion: 119 units (the raions of 23 oblasts plus Kyiv City as one unit; Luhanska and Crimea excluded). Oblast alert -> all its raions; hromada alert -> its whole raion.
at_risk_masking: No. All origins are kept in training and scoring, both alert and clear at t. Because the target is a state, this inflates short-horizon skill: +1 h Brier drops 43% against the 28-day rate. Persistence is also strong at +1 h (0.081 on validation). No onset-only or clear-at-t view is reported.
data_sources: (1) Vadimkin ukrainian-air-raid-sirens-dataset, datasets/official_data_en.csv, pinned to commit d10c80fa (2022-03-15 -> 2026-09-07), used up to 2026-09-07 00:00 UTC (last complete day 2026-09-06). (2) Reference hierarchy data/reference/regions.json (oblast->raion->hromada IDs, transliterated from regions_uk.json). (3) Weather, only for the experiment: Open-Meteo ERA5 archive (actual, 2022-03-16 -> 2026-09-06, 24 oblast centres) and the Previous Runs API '_previous_day2' day-ahead forecasts (complete from 2024-01-20). Volunteer data was compared but not used. The UkraineAlarm 48h log was not used.
data_source_variant: Official dataset only, ALL admin levels mapped to raion (union, oblast alert -> every raion, hromada -> whole raion), merged into non-overlapping intervals per raion. Snapshot pinned by commit hash with a checksum. Does NOT use alerts.in.ua or the post-2026-09-07 yellow/red regime.
preprocessing: Silver: removes exact duplicates (113,845 of 299,275 rows = 38%), drops Luhanska and Crimea, removes zero-length alerts and alerts starting after the data end, cuts alerts running at 2026-09-07 00:00 off there, and fixes rows with a raion name in the hromada field. Gold: spreads alerts to raions, merges overlaps per raion, and splits at UTC hour and day boundaries. It has every raion for every hour from 2022-03-16 to 2026-09-06, with 0 where there is no alert. No duration-based filtering: standing alerts are kept as-is on purpose.
known_label_artefacts: Duplicates: removed (38%), the same count as ours. Standing alerts: documented but NOT capped. 896 alerts > 24 h after dedup (95% in Donetska/Dnipropetrovska, Nikopol area). Two extreme hromada alerts: Lyptsi (604 days, from 2024-05-12) and Vovchansk (438 days, from 2024-05-20). The author accepts that this puts Kharkivskyi and Chuhuivskyi raions under alert 24 h/day from mid-2024 to mid-2025 ('no stuck alerts' because there is no overlapping restart inside them). This contrasts with our causal 24h cap (D-020). Recording gap 2026-08-30 -> 09-01 (inside their test window 07-13 -> 09-06): no handling found [uncertain]. A grep of the code and docs finds no gap detection or masking. The gold table fills missing hours with 0, so the gap is probably scored as 'no alert', and the 28-day/7-day shares read across it. Exactly-30-min durations: not mentioned. Oblast alert re-issued per raion at the same minute (pre-Dec-2025): documented, harmless for a union state target. Dec-2025 reform: since then, only Kyiv City still gets oblast-level alerts. Data-quality checks: strict lookups raise errors on unknown oblast/hour.
model_family: Logistic regression (scikit-learn, one model per horizon = 24 models, L2, scaled numerics, one-hot raion/oblast/hour) = final model. LightGBM (one global model over raions and horizons, log loss, early stopped at 203 trees) = challenger, not adopted: its gain over LR was +0.4% (CI -0.5 .. 1.2%), and the choice rule needs a gain larger than the bootstrap uncertainty.
features: All computed at the origin from data before it. State: alert_now (from merged intervals), spell_hours (current alert or quiet spell length, capped at 48 h for LR), alerts_24h (starts in the last 24 h). History: share of the last 1, 3, 6, 24, 168, 672 h under alert, origin hour excluded (672 h = the 28-day-rate baseline, so the model can start from it). Spatial context: share of the raion's oblast and of the whole country under alert now (no neighbour/border table). Calendar: hour of day and weekday of the TARGET hour in Kyiv local time, plus the horizon. Kyiv vs UTC tested once on validation: 3.3% vs 3.1% skill, Kyiv kept. IDs: raion and oblast as categories. LightGBM importance: 28-day share 59%, 7-day share 20%, target hour 7%. External: weather (wind, gusts, log1p precipitation, low cloud, temperature at the oblast centre at the target hour), tested only as an experiment and not adopted.
external_feature_timing: Exemplary two-stage weather design. Stage 1 = ORACLE: actual ERA5 weather at the target hour. It is deliberately leaky and labelled 'upper bound, uses future weather, not a result'. ERA5 is also published about 5 days late, so it could not be used live even for past hours. Stage 2 = clean forecasts: the Open-Meteo Previous Runs '_previous_day2' value, from a run started at least 48 h before the target hour, so at least 24 h before the origin. The code assumes publication within 12 h and checks every row (weather_models.check_published). '_previous_day1' was rejected as unsafe at h = 24. The Historical Forecast API was rejected because it joins the newest run per hour, which is after the origin. Open-Meteo's end-of-hour stamping was aligned (value stamped 01:00 = hour 00:00-01:00). A stop rule (oracle gain < 1% and CI includes 0) was set before running. The oracle gain was -0.02% (-0.21 .. +0.21%), so stage 2 was never run: a forecast cannot carry more information than the truth.
ablation_design: Yes, matched. The with/without-weather comparison uses the same 4.27M training rows (same seed), the same model and settings, and the same validation rows. The no-weather row reproduces the main model exactly (3.35%), which shows the rows match. The paired skill difference (with vs without) gets its own day-block bootstrap CI, overall and per alert-rate band. Kyiv vs UTC calendar and LightGBM vs LR are also paired on the same rows. Caveat (stated by the author): the weather enters the LR only linearly per horizon; LightGBM was not tried with weather. The sample is not time-restricted to the weather-forecast era (from 2024-01-21) for the oracle stage, because ERA5 covers everything.
split_scheme: Chronological fixed splits by date, half-open [start, end), UTC. Train 2022-03-16 -> 2026-05-17. Validation 2026-05-18 -> 2026-07-12 (8 weeks). Test 2026-07-13 -> 2026-09-06 (8 weeks, scored once). An origin belongs to a split only if all 24 target hours fall inside it (a purge), and it needs at least 28 days of history. Training origins = a random third of hours, each with one random horizon from each of the bands 1-8, 9-16, 17-24 (4.27M rows); a full 24-horizon expansion (34M rows) does not fit in memory. Test = every hour (rolling origin, 1,321 origins x 119 raions x 24 h = 3.77M forecasts). The final model is REFIT on train + validation (2022-04-13 -> 2026-07-11, 4.43M rows) before the test. No refits within the test.
metrics: Brier score (main), overall and per horizon 1-24. Brier skill score vs the 28-day rate, overall and per alert-rate band (<10%, 10-20%, 20-60%, >=60% of hours). The bands are measured over the 12 weeks BEFORE the split (for test: 2026-04-20 -> 2026-07-12), never from the split itself. Secondary: log loss, ROC-AUC, reliability diagram. No PR-AUC [uncertain].
unit_of_metric: Pooled over raions x origins x horizons; additionally pooled within alert-rate bands. No within-unit averaged AUC reported.
baseline_strength: Baselines: persistence (state at origin for all 24 h), 28-day rate (share of the last 28 days under alert; the 'baseline to beat', a rolling recent rate), and hour-of-day rate (same, only the target hour of day). No calibrated persistence; no climatology fit on train. Test skill vs the 28-day rate: LR +3.6% (CI 1.5 .. 6.5%); hour-of-day -1.3%; persistence -71% overall, but persistence beats the 28-day rate at +1 h (0.087 vs 0.107). On a state target, persistence at +1 h is a strong reference that the skill vs the 28-day rate hides. LR +1 h 0.061 beats persistence 0.087.
calibration: Reliability diagrams on validation and test (reports/reliability.png, reports/final_test_reliability.png). The author reports both models well calibrated. No post-hoc calibration fitted.
calibration_under_drift: Not explicitly tested. No calibration-in-the-large comparison test vs validation, no recalibration. The base rate shift is noted descriptively: 34% of hours under alert in test, and test weeks are 'more uneven' with wider CIs. The post-2026-09-07 regime is not evaluated.
uncertainty_of_gain: Yes. Day-block bootstrap (1,000 resamples, whole UTC days, because forecasts from neighbouring origins overlap) gives 95% intervals on the skill vs the 28-day rate, overall and per band. A paired bootstrap on model-vs-model differences (LightGBM vs LR, weather vs no weather) drives the choice rules. No Diebold-Mariano test.
regime_coverage: Train spans 2022 -> mid-May 2026, so it covers the Jan-2025 drone surge and the Dec-2025 raion-level reform. Both validation and test fall after the reform (raion-only alerts except Kyiv City), which suits a raion target. The author documents the reform as a data finding. The Sep-2026 yellow/red reform is not covered: the data ends 2026-09-07 and no API data is used.
leakage_handling: Causal features: share windows shift by one hour, so the origin hour is excluded. State comes from intervals that started before the origin. The hour-of-day rate uses only earlier days. Tests: test_features_do_not_change_when_the_future_changes (truncation-style), test_state_at_origin_uses_only_the_past, test_share_excludes_the_origin_hour, test_origin_split_needs_all_24_target_hours_inside (purge), and a horizon-labelling test. Weather has test_weather_features_do_not_change_when_the_future_changes, which also checks that the oracle features DO move: a working negative control, like our test_leakage requirement. The bands for skill reporting are computed before the split. Possible gaps: (1) the 2026-08-30 -> 09-01 recording gap seems to be treated as no-alert inside the test, which corrupts both labels and rolling shares [uncertain]. (2) LightGBM early stopping on validation makes its validation score slightly optimistic (acknowledged). (3) Alerts cut at the data end are known only at the end, which is harmless here. (4) Standing alerts use observed end times. That is causal for a state target (the alert is genuinely active), but their 600-day state dominates some raions.
test_window_hygiene: Good, and documented. The test was scored once (python -m pipeline final). The code was committed and pushed before the run (commit 1a87ca9). The pipeline was checked by reproducing the validation result exactly with the final code before scoring test. The weather branch never touched test. Choice rules (LGBM vs LR; the weather stop rule) were fixed before seeing the results. No pre-registration document beyond PROBLEM.md, but the decisions there are dated. All work happened on 2026-10-12 (single day), so the target changed mid-day (daily 7-day -> hourly 24 h) before modelling.
headline_results: Test (2026-07-13 -> 09-06), LR: Brier 0.1033 vs 28-day rate 0.1072, skill +3.6% (95% CI 1.5 .. 6.5%). Positive in every band: <10% +1.9%, 10-20% +4.7%, 20-60% +2.3%, >=60% +5.7%; all CIs above 0. By horizon: +1 h Brier 0.061 vs 0.107 (43% skill), +2 h 9%, +6 h 2.5%, +24 h 0.7%. Validation: LR 3.3% (2.3 .. 4.4%), LightGBM 3.7% (2.1 .. 5.3%). Weather oracle on validation: -0.02% (-0.21 .. +0.21%), so it gives no gain. An extra raw-data check: in 2025-2026, the share of hours under alert falls from 32.6% (calmest fifth of hours) to 26.3% (gustiest), but the rate of NEW alerts stays flat at 5.4-5.9%. Weather relates to place/season, not to onset timing. It beats naive baselines, but almost all of the gain is the persistence of ongoing alerts at +1-2 h; beyond about 8 h it is about 1% better than the 28-day rate.
code_available: Yes, public on GitHub. Python 3.13, pinned requirements (pandas 3.0.6, scikit-learn 1.9.1, lightgbm 4.7.0, etc.). Medallion pipeline (bronze/silver/gold/features), `python -m pipeline`, pytest tests per step, generated data not committed, dataset commit pinned. No license. Deadline-day project, not maintained after 2026-10-12.
takeaways_for_project: 1) The weather oracle -> forecast template is directly reusable for any external feature we might add (ISW, launches, weather). Run a deliberately leaky oracle upper bound first, on the SAME rows and seed. Set the stop rule (gain < threshold or CI includes 0) before running. Skip the clean stage if the oracle fails. Use '_previous_day2'-style vintage selection, checked row-by-row against the publication time. This fits our 'no dependency without approval' and leakage rules (CLAUDE.md features). 2) Their raw-data finding that weather moves the share of time under alert but not the NEW-alert rate (5.4-5.9% flat) is evidence that weather is unlikely to help our ONSET target. Cite it if weather is proposed. 3) A state target hides the onset problem: 43% of +1 h skill is persistence. That confirms our masking choice (Target section, D-020 estimand) and shows why our numbers will look much lower than theirs. Do not compare headline skills across repos. 4) Their uncapped standing alerts (Lyptsi 604 d, Vovchansk 438 d) make Kharkivskyi/Chuhuivskyi raions 24 h/day for a year. This independently confirms the problem D-020 solves. 5) They did not mask the 2026-08-30 -> 09-01 recording gap inside their test. This supports our D-013 gap mask as a differentiator worth stating in the README [uncertain]. 6) Day-block bootstrap with paired model-vs-model CIs and a 'beat by more than the uncertainty' choice rule maps to our D-013 week-block bootstrap. 7) Alert-rate bands measured on the 12 weeks before the split are a leak-free stratification alternative to our fixed frontline/rear/Kyiv groups. 8) Their refit on train+val before the test is the opposite of our D-021 'no refit after early stopping'. Note the trade-off but keep ours. 9) 'Reproduce validation exactly with the final code, commit, push, then score test once' is a cheap hygiene step that fits our M4 protocol.
best_practices: Adopt: pin the dataset commit + checksum. Use a two-stage oracle/clean ablation for external features with a pre-set stop rule. Run paired ablations on identical rows (same seed) and confirm the baseline row reproduces. Use a day/week-block bootstrap for overlapping forecasts. Use choice rules tied to the CI. Write a future-change truncation test whose negative control (oracle features) must move. Compute strata from the pre-split window only. Commit code before the single test run. Check null results for silent failure (strict joins raise, completeness checks, a timestamp-alignment sanity check via the temperature peak hour). State the limitations of the gain plainly. Avoid / anti-patterns: a state target without at-risk masking, reported as headline skill. Persistence-at-+1 h dominance is hidden behind skill vs the 28-day rate. Standing multi-hundred-day alerts are accepted uncapped. Recording gaps are filled as 0 inside the test window [uncertain]. Validation scores after early stopping on validation are optimistic (they acknowledge this). Training rows are subsampled to random horizons for memory, which changes the training distribution; this is fine but should be stated. There is no PR-AUC or within-unit AUC for imbalanced quiet raions.
